world.note: Provisional bounds. Bohemia’s scripts place coordinates as far east as X 16000 m, so the terrain is at least that wide. The exact size will be read from the official areaflags.map header or the terrain configuration; it is not derived from the advertised 267 km².

grid.note: The GPS shows 3-digit numbers on the terrain’s Grid Zoom1 step (100 m on every official terrain checked). Which edge the second number counts from differs between terrains (Chernarus+ south, Livonia north), so Nasdara’s direction stays unverified until the terrain configuration or an in-game reading confirms it.

features.name: Border crossing
notes: Region boundary from Bohemia’s location-music script (2 rectangles).
Bohemia’s Dev Blog Recap (2) shows a vehicle crossing the “Dar-e Ardis border crossing”. The scripts define one border-crossing zone, so this is probably it, but no official source states the link.

features.name: Desert
notes: Region boundary from Bohemia’s location-music script (2 rectangles).
Bohemia’s wildlife dev blog says desert monitors mostly live in the “Dasht-e Sarman Desert”. These eastern desert zones are likely that desert, but the scripts only call them “Desert”.
Rectangles are music regions drawn by Bohemia, so edges are approximate and one reaches past X 16,000 m.

area.note: Six regions defined in Bohemia’s 1.30 scripts. More named areas come from the terrain configuration.

settlement.note: Town and village names with positions are in the terrain configuration inside the installed game. Bohemia has not published them separately.

landmark.note: Hills, viewpoints and other named landmarks come from the terrain configuration (installed game).

water.note: Well and pump positions are expected in Bohemia’s Nasdara mission files (not yet published on 2026-10-15). Wells without loot points may only be listed in the terrain object data.

military.note: Military buildings come from Bohemia’s mission files (not yet published).

police.note: Police stations come from Bohemia’s mission files (not yet published).

fire.note: Fire stations come from Bohemia’s mission files (not yet published).

medical.note: Medical buildings come from Bohemia’s mission files (not yet published).

fuel.note: Fuel stations come from Bohemia’s mission files (not yet published).

industrial.note: Industrial sites come from Bohemia’s mission files. The oil-refinery region is available now as a named area.

farm.note: Farm buildings come from Bohemia’s mission files (not yet published).

bunker.note: Urban bunker positions are expected in the mission file cfgbunkerbroadcast.json (read by the 1.30 scripts).

tunnel.note: Irrigation tunnel entrances are rebuildable structures; positions are expected in the mission or terrain data.

underground.note: Underground areas come from cfgundergroundtriggers.json in the mission files.

building.note: All loot buildings come from mapgrouppos.xml in the mission files.

spawn-vehicle.note: Possible vehicle spawns come from cfgeventspawns.xml in the mission files.

spawn-event.note: Possible event spawns come from cfgeventspawns.xml in the mission files.

spawn-wildlife.note: Wildlife territories come from the env folder of the mission files.

spawn-player.note: Player spawn points come from cfgplayerspawnpoints.xml.

hazard.note: Static hazard areas come from cfgeffectarea.json; possible dynamic areas from cfgeventspawns.xml.

mechanics.title: Wells and pumps give clean water
mechanics.text: In the 1.30 scripts every structure of the Well class (wells, hand pumps and water-cistern truck wrecks) supplies clean water and allows drinking, filling, washing and wetting clothes.

mechanics.title: Brick wells work only after rebuilding
mechanics.text: Nasdara’s brick wells (Land_WaterWell_Brick) return no water until their roof part is rebuilt; after that they give clean water and drinking uses a bucket action. Their state is per server, so this app shows availability as unknown until you record an observation.

mechanics.title: Water for cooling and rebuilding
mechanics.text: Bohemia says water is needed to cool down and to rinse sand from your eyes after a sandstorm. Wells support washing your head and wetting clothes, and mortar for rebuilding is mixed at a well.

mechanics.title: Urban bunkers and Morse broadcasts
mechanics.text: Radio transmissions in Morse code carry coordinates and access codes for urban bunkers. In the scripts the bunker list is read from the mission file cfgbunkerbroadcast.json, which Bohemia has not published yet.

mechanics.title: Regional wildlife
mechanics.text: Nasdara adds mouflons, desert monitors (mostly in the Dasht-e Sarman Desert) and territorial dog packs that stay near specific places, mainly military zones.

mechanics.title: Heat, sandstorms and new conditions
mechanics.text: Sandstorms, heatstroke and silicosis are new threats on Nasdara. Proper gear, shade and water help manage them.
